cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

p.em: Example: Navigating a mixed-up world requires inner clarity.

cosy-blockquote.p: Guidance – advice or information aimed at resolving a problem.

p.em: Example: When feeling lost, we look for moral guidance from trusted allies.

cosy-blockquote.p: Contradiction – a combination of statements or ideas that are opposed.

p.em: Example: Life is full of contradiction, blending joy and hardship.

cosy-blockquote.p: Faith – complete trust or confidence in someone or something.

p.em: Example: Keeping faith in good outcomes helps us weather bad days.

cosy-blockquote.p: Cynicism – an inclination to believe that people are motivated by self-interest.

p.em: Example: Guard your heart against falling into bitter cynicism.

cosy-blockquote.p: Control – the power to influence or direct people's behavior.

p.em: Example: When the world feels chaotic, focus on what you can control.

cosy-blockquote.p: Strength – the quality or state of being physically or mentally strong.

p.em: Example: True inner strength shows when standing up after a fall.

cosy-blockquote.p: Tough – strong and durable; able to endure hardship.

p.em: Example: She proved to be tough enough to handle unexpected changes.

cosy-blockquote.p: Low – feeling depressed, pessimistic, or lacking energy.

p.em: Example: It is natural to feel low when plans fail, but hope returns.

cosy-blockquote.p: Insane – extremely foolish, irrational, or chaotic.

p.em: Example: Sometimes the news makes the world appear completely insane.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Share whether you agree or disagree with these statements and discuss them with your teacher:

ul.li: Incorrect: It is a messed world → Correct: It is a mixed-up world ((Use the established compound adjective 'mixed-up'.))
Incorrect: You have got be → Correct: You have got to be ((Include 'to' before the infinitive verb after 'have got'.))
Incorrect: I feel lowly → Correct: I feel low ((Use 'low' as an adjective for sad or lacking energy; 'lowly' means humble.))
